# Bernhard Haslhofer

> Bernhard Haslhofer leads the Digital Currency Ecosystems research group at the Complexity Science Hub (CSH) in Vienna, Austria. His research develops computational methods for cryptoasset analytics and decentralized finance (DeFi), digital crime and forensics, and large-scale disinformation. He co-founded Iknaio Cryptoasset Analytics, is a court-certified expert in IT and cryptoasset forensics, and teaches at TU Wien.

Key facts:
- Affiliation: Complexity Science Hub Vienna (https://www.csh.ac.at/), research group leader
- Co-founder and Head of Research: Iknaio Cryptoasset Analytics (https://www.iknaio.com/)
- Creator of the open-source GraphSense cryptoasset analytics platform (https://graphsense.org/)
- Founding editor of the Open Blockchain Intelligence Standards (OBIS) initiative (https://obistandards.org/)
- Research methods co-developed with the Bavarian Central Office for the Prosecution of Cybercrime supported an international law enforcement operation that took down over 373,000 illegal dark web sites (Europol, 2026); the takedown itself was carried out by law enforcement
- ORCID: https://orcid.org/0000-0002-0415-4491
- Google Scholar: https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=15K0uBUAAAAJ
- Contact: haslhofer@csh.ac.at

## Research areas

- Cryptoasset Analytics & DeFi: quantitative methods for measuring cryptoasset ecosystems and DeFi protocols at scale, from tracing fund flows across ledgers to analyzing investment strategies, risks, and structural dependencies; recent work examines stablecoin flows and their behavior under stress
- Digital Crime & Forensics: algorithms and open tools for tracing illicit fund flows and analyzing dark web ecosystems, producing forensic evidence that supports criminal investigations and prosecutions; current projects develop LLM-based methods for data analysis in law enforcement and advance open blockchain intelligence standards (OBIS)
- Large-Scale Disinformation: network-analytic methods for understanding how disinformation spreads through online ecosystems and how coordinated campaigns can be detected at scale
